headline: Pretrained protein language models are adapted with task-specific data and priors for prediction and design
label: Adapting Pretrained Biomolecular Language Models
summary: Preprints adapt pretrained protein language models to antimicrobial, expression and resistance tasks, using fine-tuning and annotation priors under strict evaluation splits.
synthesis: The dominant thread is adapting pretrained sequence models to specific biological tasks through fine-tuning or added priors. Multi-task LoRA on ESM-2 jointly predicts AMP potency and hemolytic toxicity under 60% homology splits. XAMPGen fine-tunes ProGen on known antimicrobial peptides and applies probing classifiers and self-attention analysis for interpretation. BacLLM fuses UniProt annotation priors into protein language models for AMR analysis, and ESMC-MonoYield is trained on a 39,000-protein E. coli yield assay. The kinase-library study applies a related prior-refinement logic, filtering expanded kinase-substrate relationships by protein association to improve activity inference. The pocket coengagement work is the least aligned, scoring drug pairs by shared pocket engagement. The items are heterogeneous; the shared advance is explicit conditioning on task data, annotations or constraints rather than generic embeddings.
